objective: maximize cumulative user profit while enforcing verified-publication hard minimums and minimizing user intervention

hardPublicationPolicy.rule: Expected-profit optimization may choose WHICH qualified products to publish, but may not reduce the verified-publication floor or erase carried debt.

pcAvailabilityPolicy.assumption: User normally closes Windows PC after 01:00 JST.
pcAvailabilityPolicy.after0100: Do not require Windows publisher execution. Continue cloud research, build preparation, queue/state/ledger repair and fallback preparation.
pcAvailabilityPolicy.frontLoadRule: Debt and current-day publication minimums must be pushed toward verified public state before 01:00; do not depend on post-01:00 local execution.

amplificationPolicy.confirmedWinnerRule: A confirmed winner requires observed performance evidence such as sales, PV/CVR, acquisitions, installs or repeat usage. Asset count alone is not demand evidence.
amplificationPolicy.currentState: No confirmed paid or Store winner can be declared because BOOTH sales, note sales/PV and Microsoft Store acquisition/install/CVR data are absent.

provisionalClusterOrder.reason: Strongest coherent cross-channel asset density plus lowest incremental bundle cost: two verified BOOTH assets, two verified paid note articles and four free tools cover one operational buyer journey.
One verified BOOTH OS, one verified paid note article and four complementary free tools cover distinct stages of one research workflow.
Four free tools form a coherent acquisition cluster, but paid handover assets are still unverified and therefore this cluster must not be over-expanded yet.

amplificationPolicy.actionRule: Use provisional clusters only for low-cost, functionally distinct experiments and bundles. Do not create a large series until actual demand metrics confirm the cluster.
amplificationPolicy.measurementRule: Prioritize capture of product-level BOOTH sales, note sales/PV/likes, Microsoft Store page views/acquisitions/installs/CVR and measurable referral/campaign identifiers from free tools.

runPlan.goal: Service debt first; if blocked, switch quickly to the strongest low-cost provisional amplification experiment: event+sponsor bundle or its distinct follow-up article.
Continue verified-publication recovery while preserving distinct buyer value; do not infer winner status from asset density.
Prefer coherent adjacent products over unrelated novelty; event risk must be clearly deeper than the existing event operations OS.
Only expand the small-organization cluster with clear RACI/load/backup-owner differentiation; avoid duplicating handover checklists.
Use the thesis/research cluster as the second provisional amplification path if stronger quota candidates are already handled.
Late catch-up with distinct high-intent adjacent products; sponsor tracker must focus on post-contract fulfillment.
Final PC-dependent recovery window before 01:00; verify formally or carry exact residual debt forward without clearing it.

productionRunPolicy.normalCompletion: At least one newly verified public artifact per PC-available production run when debt or quota remains, with multiple publications encouraged when safe qualified candidates are ready.
productionRunPolicy.blockedCandidate: Diagnose briefly; if strict publication cannot be reached, defer and switch to another qualified candidate rather than ending the run.
nonCompletionEvidence: HTTP/title-only evidence when commerce checks are required

crossChannelAssetSignals: Event+sponsor cluster: verified BOOTH event operations OS and sponsor CRM; verified paid note sponsor-pipeline and event-manual articles; free event-checklist, event-reception-calc, sponsor-plan-calc and sponsor-email-maker tools.
Thesis cluster: verified BOOTH thesis progress OS; verified paid note thesis progress article; four free thesis planning/diagnosis tools.
Small-organization cluster: free handover, role-assignment, meeting-action and agenda-timebox tools; paid handover BOOTH/note assets remain unverified and cannot yet support a winner claim.
external: note official analysis of about 300k paid articles reports paid-article sales +26.8% YoY and creator count +42.0% YoY; AI utilization +268.6%, SNS/content operations +258.7%, side jobs/remote work +179.0%.
Microsoft states the Store serves over 250 million monthly active users and allows non-game apps to use their own commerce and retain 100% of revenue.
Current Store search surfaced many generic image-resizer/compressor and file-renamer competitors, while CSV cleanup appeared less directly crowded in Japanese search results.

profitRules: Debt and today's verified-publication floor are first priority.
Within that floor, prefer stronger purchase intent, differentiation, conversion fit and expected net profit.
Use existing public assets to create coherent bundles before inventing unrelated BOOTH products.
Do not publish plaintext paid assets to GitHub.
Do not infer public URLs; independently verify them before marking completed or linking funnels.
Use actual sales/message evidence when available; do not invent demand metrics.
Avoid low-value near duplicates; switch to a distinct qualified fallback when needed.
Do not call a provisional cluster a winner until observed performance evidence exists.
Do not reactivate KDP or LINE without explicit user instruction.

MicrosoftStore.status: initial app publication route proven; next research priority is a local-first CSV cleanup/deduplication utility; no repository performance metrics available yet
